mentions.name: PAPER
mentions.description: A Python package installer designed from the ground up to avoid Pip's design mistakes, taking advantage of new packaging standards and offering Pipx-like functionality. Unlike uv or Poetry it is not a project manager or workflow tool: it installs the packages (and dependencies) you ask for, when and where you ask. It provides a programmatic API via a separate wheel (no subprocess-to-CLI needed), installs cross-environment, targets a ~1MB base disk footprint with aggressive caching and hard-linking, bootstraps itself as a zipapp with no hidden vendored dependencies, supports optional dependencies for non-essential functionality, and uses a CLI of separate hyphenated commands rather than subcommands.
mentions.problem: Existing installers like Pip are large and slow, and force other tools to shell out to a CLI instead of offering a programmatic API; PAPER avoids these design mistakes.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm developing PAPER (the Python Application, Package and Environment wRangler, a Python package installer)
